text:
SURAH AD-DUKHAN
Number of verses: 59 | Period: Mecca (circa the 7th-8th years of revelation) | Pedagogical order: 85
Subject: Economic Crisis — The Psychology of Historical Warnings
Reference Frame: Qur'an Tafsir Reference Protocol v27 | Foundational Axiom: an-Nisa 136 | Epistemic Limit: Allah knows best.
THE PROTOCOL FRAME AND THE ONTOLOGICAL GROUND
The Foundational Axiom (an-Nisa 136): this analysis proceeds upon the ground of faith in Allah, in His Prophet, in the Book He sent down upon His Prophet, and in the books He sent down before. No interpretation can bring these four pillars to collapse. The analysis of Surah ad-Dukhan, remaining within this ontological frame, aims to bring to light the consciousness of justice, liberty, and responsibility (taqwa) that the revelation offers to humanity.
The Surah's Context of Revelation (0a-0b): Surah ad-Dukhan was sent down in the middle of the Meccan period, in approximately the 7th-8th years of the revelation. According to the report of Ibn Mas'ud, the surah was revealed in the time of famine lived through in Mecca. In the el-Kashshaf (Zamakhshari) it is stated that the surah was revealed in Mecca and that it has 59 verses.
THE FIRST GROUP: AD-DUKHAN 1-6 — THE CLEAR BOOK AND THE BLESSED NIGHT (THE EPISTEMOLOGICAL GROUND OF REVELATION)
The Translation (el-Kashshaf):
1. “Ha, Mim.”
2. “By the Clear Book I swear”
3. “We sent it down upon a blessed night. Surely We are the warners.”
4. “In it every wise affair is separated.”
5. “As a command from Our presence. Surely We are the senders.”
6. “As a mercy from your Lord. Surely He is the Hearer, the Knower.”
Etymological-Semantic Analysis:
“Ha, Mim”: the huruf-i mufassala (the separated letters). According to Zeccac's assessment in the Ma'ani'l-Qur'an, these letters draw attention to the building blocks of the Arabic language and carry the message: “This book is composed of the most basic units of your language; and yet you cannot bring the like of it.” The rational counterpart: the revelation has been built from material the addressee knows; but the structure produced from that material lies beyond the productive capacity of the addressee. This is an epistemological challenge.
“Kitab-i Mubin”: the word “mubin” comes from the root B-Y-N. Zeccac defines this root as “to bring out into the open the side of a thing that remained hidden, to remove ambiguity.” “Mubin” does not only mean “clear”; it means “that which also makes other things clear, that discloses.” Its semantic field: transparency, verifiability, accessibility. In the jahiliyya, knowledge was in the monopoly of the soothsayers and the elite; the attribute “mubin” proclaims the breaking of that monopoly.
“Layla-i mubarak”: the word “night” (layl) in Qur'anic semantics represents the state of darkness, ignorance, and indeterminacy. “Mubarak” comes from the root B-R-K; Zeccac explains it as “the good that is fixed, that strikes root, that continues by increase.” The rational counterpart: the revelation is a process of enlightenment that cleaves the darkness of ignorance. This “night” is not a single calendar night; it is the very process of the revelation's 22 years and 6 months — that is, humanity's passage from darkness to light. The “blessing” expresses the ever-increasing, rooting, good-turning energy of that process.
“Yufrazu kullu emrin hakim”: F-R-Q, coming from the same root as “Furqan,” means “to separate, to distinguish right from falsehood.” “Amr” here means “affair, decree, ordering.” “Hakim” comes from the root H-K-M: “wise, measured, each thing in its place.” Zeccac explains the word “amr” as “decree and governance.” The rational counterpart: in the process of revelation, every wise affair (justice, law, morality, economy) is separated one from another; that is, a system is established in which right is separated from falsehood, justice from oppression, the straight from the crooked. This is not a fatalist “writing of destiny” but the instituting of the systemic laws of the divine pedagogy (Sunnatullah).
“Rahma”: the root R-H-M is connected with the maternal womb; it expresses protective, encompassing, unconditional love and compassion. The revelation is positioned not as an instrument of punishment but as an instrument of mercy (protection, encompassing, compassion).
Rational Analysis:
These six verses establish the epistemological ground of the revelation. The message is this: the source of knowledge is not human speculation but a divine transfer. But this transfer has been given in the language the addressee will understand (Arabic), with the concepts of the age the addressee lived in. The metaphor of “night” represents the ignorance, the tribal wars, and the order of exploitation of seventh-century Arabia. The “blessed night” is the moment at which that order began to be transformed by the revelation. The “separation of every wise affair” is the separating of the legal, moral, and economic system the revelation brought from the jahiliyya confusion.
As required by article 20a of the Protocol (tanZih), the expression “the separation of affairs on that night” cannot be understood as Allah's sitting at a table and writing destiny. This is the symbolic telling of the divine will's operating through universal laws (Sunnatullah).
Structural Sociology:
In the social structure of Mecca, knowledge was in the monopoly of the Quraysh aristocracy (the mala'). The soothsayers, the poets, and the elders controlled knowledge and sustained the social hierarchy through this monopoly of knowledge. The attribute “mubin” (clear, disclosing) is a structural intervention in that knowledge monopoly. Now knowledge comes from a source open, transparent, and verifiable to all. This is the epistemological dimension of the principle of “power and deviation” in article 1a of the Protocol: religion corrects the deviation of power by democratizing knowledge.
Maqasid Detail:
The maqsad of this group is to establish the authority and the epistemological legitimacy of the revelation. The aim is to say to the addressee: “This message has been built from material you know (Arabic); but the structure it produces is beyond your capacity. It comes from a divine source, and its aim is to warn you, to protect you, and to enlighten you.”
In the light of articles 3a (the Common Misunderstanding: the Reduction of Worship to Ritual), 17a (Symbolic Language), and 29 (Structural Sociology) of the Protocol, this is the clearest proof that the Qur'an is not “a book of calendars and nights” but “a manifesto of systemic transformation and the building of civilization.”
To read the “night” as a twelve-hour astronomical span of time, and to hope that the systemic sins committed all through the year (interest, exploitation, the violation of the rights of others, injustice) will be erased in this single night “with tears and ritual,” is wholly contrary to the Qur'anic principles of Taqwa (the Consciousness of Responsibility) and Salih Amal (Systemic Goodness).
1. The Semantic Revolution: “Night” (Layl) and Ontological Darkness (Zulumat)
In Qur'anic terminology “night” and “darkness” (zulumat) are not merely the setting of the sun; they are the symbol of the jahiliyya, of ignorance, of oppression, of superstition, and of the absence of divine guidance (the Furqan) (for example: al-Baqara 257 — from the darknesses to the light).
The “Blessed Night” in ad-Dukhan 3 expresses the moment at which the revelation (the Nur) first burst open within the ontological and sociological darkness (the jahiliyya system) into which seventh-century Arabia and all humanity had sunk — that is, the epoch of the enlightenment revolution that would last some twenty-three years.
This night is “mubarak” (blessed / ever-increasing, striking root and turning to good), because it is not an event that ends in a single night; it is the beginning of the twenty-three-year divine pedagogy that would carry humanity from slavery to freedom, from jahiliyya to justice, from tribalism to universal law.
2. The Sociological Trap of the Traditional Reading
Why the human mind turns to the search for “a single sacred night” can be set upon a rational ground through article 14c of the Protocol (the Neuroscientific Frame):
The Limbic System's Search for the “Shortcut”: the limbic system of the human brain (the center of pleasure, fear, and comfort) flees from an arduous process that requires continual moral effort (taqwa) and a systemic struggle for justice (salih amal). In its place, the idea of “the forgiveness of all sins” through an intense ritual performed one night a year is, for the limbic system, a perfect “psychological mechanism of escape and relief.”
The Preservation of the Status Quo: if a merchant commits fraud in trade all through the year, sustains the order of exploitation with interest (riba), and crushes the weak; but believes that when the “Blessed Night” comes he will be forgiven with weeping — then religion has become a cosmetic instrument that covers over oppression. Article 1c of the Protocol (the True Function of Commands and Prohibitions) objects to this categorically. The Qur'an came down to demolish the superstitions that invent such “magical nights of forgiveness” and make people flee from responsibility (from the day of reckoning).
THE SECOND GROUP: AD-DUKHAN 7-16 — DENIAL, DOUBT, AND THE SYSTEMIC CONSEQUENCE
The Translation (el-Kashshaf):
7. “He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, if you are of certain faith.”
8. “There is no god but Him. He gives life and causes to die. He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.”
9. “No; they are playing in doubt.”
10. “Watch for the day when the heaven brings an evident smoke.”
11. “It will envelop the people. This is a searing punishment.”
12. “Our Lord! Remove the punishment from us. Surely we are believers.”
13. “Where now is their taking of lesson? Yet a clear messenger had come to them.”
14. “Then they turned from him and said, 'A taught madman!'”
15. “We shall remove the punishment a little. Surely you are those who turn back.”
16. “On the day We seize with the great seizure — surely We are the takers of recompense.”
Etymological-Semantic Analysis:
“Shakkin yal'abun”: “shakk” means “doubt, the refusing of faith on account of hesitation”; but the critical word here is “yal'abun” — “they play.” The root L-'-B means “play, amusement, the not taking seriously.” Zeccac explains this usage as “to treat a serious matter as a game.” The semantic message: denial is not an intellectual position but a psychological escape. The addressee's problem is not lack of knowledge but the unwillingness to take responsibility.
“Dukhan”: the root D-H-N means “smoke.” Zeccac defines it as “the substance that rises after burning, that suffocates, that covers the sight.” The symbolic counterpart: smoke carries both a physical meaning (the dust cloud of the famine period, the hallucination hunger produced) and a metaphorical one (a state that covers the truth, that shuts off sight, that suffocates). The rational counterpart: the “blurring of vision” and the “suffocating atmosphere” produced by the system of oppression and denial.
“Muntaqimun”: the root N-Q-M. This word must be read within the frame of article 20a of the Protocol (tanZih). The literal reading of Allah's “taking vengeance” is not a human wrath or rancor. It is an error to confine the abstract/symbolic telling to the concrete/literal. Zeccac explains the root N-Q-M as “to make one live fully the consequences of a thing, to give its return without deficiency.” The rational counterpart: the operating of Sunnatullah (the universal law). It is the collapse of the system of oppression through its own contradictions. The person who opposes gravity prepares his own oppression, his own being crushed beneath the law. Justice, too, is Allah's unchanging law, which cannot be altered. “Vengeance” here is the symbolic expression of the inevitable manifestation of justice. The law of justice operates, and oppression collapses beneath its own weight.
“Al-batshatu'l-kubra”: B-T-S means “to grasp with violence, to seize.” “Kubra” means “the greatest.” This may point to a historical event (Badr or the conquest of Mecca), and likewise expresses in general the inevitable collapse of the system of oppression.
Rational Analysis:
The rational core of this group is this: when the truth comes, to reject it is not an intellectual choice but a psychological escape (“they play in doubt”). This escape is, on the individual plane, “cognitive dissonance,” and on the social plane, the “reflex of preserving the status quo.” If the Meccan aristocracy accepted the egalitarian message the revelation brought, it would lose its economic and social privileges. For this reason it marginalizes the truth with the label “madman.”
The metaphor of “smoke” is the suffocating atmosphere produced by the system of oppression. When a society deviates from justice, “smoke” settles upon it: sight is blurred, breathing grows hard, direction is lost. This operates both on the individual plane (torment of conscience, crisis of meaning) and on the social (chaos, insecurity, ecological destruction).
The expression “Remove the punishment; we shall believe” must be read with the principle of “ran” (neuroplasticity) in article 14e of the Protocol: repeated denial destroys mental flexibility. To say “we shall believe” in the moment of crisis is not a true transformation but the panic reaction of the limbic system. For this reason the expression “you are those who turn back” announces that this reaction is not lasting, that the old habits will return.
Structural Sociology:
The economic structure of Mecca was built upon the trade monopoly of the Quraysh aristocracy. The principles the revelation brought — “justice in measure and weight” (Protocol 30b), “the protection of the orphan's property,” and “infak” — directly threatened this economic structure. The metaphor of “smoke” represents the social suffocation this economic system produced. The gulf between rich and poor enwraps the social fabric like “a suffocating smoke.”
Within the frame of article 29 of the Protocol (Structural Sociology): the message of tawhid is not only a theological revolution but a structural sociological revolution that demolishes tribal/class superiority. The expression “the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them” proclaims that no human power can claim absolute authority (Protocol 10c).
Maqasid Detail:
The maqsad of this group is to expose the psychological and sociological mechanism of denial and to announce the inevitable end of the system of oppression. The word “vengeance” must be read, within the frame of the tanZih principle, as the manifestation of justice. The aim is not to frighten but to warn: “Oppression is not sustainable; it will collapse through its own contradictions.” The human-like understanding of Allah is the product of literal reading. Allah is the possessor of absolute justice and infinite mercy. Vengeance and Allah cannot be thought together. These literal readings that force the symbolic meaning to the point of ascribing slander to Allah must be rejected.
THE THIRD GROUP: AD-DUKHAN 17-33 — THE PHARAOH PARADIGM (HISTORICAL ARCHETYPE AND SYSTEMIC COLLAPSE)
The Translation (el-Kashshaf):
17. “We tested the people of Pharaoh before them. A noble messenger came to them.”
18. “Give me Allah's servants. Surely I am a trustworthy messenger to you.”
19. “Do not grow arrogant against Allah. Surely I bring you a clear proof.”
20. “Surely I have taken refuge in my Lord, who is your Lord also, from your stoning me.”
21. “If you do not believe in me, keep away from me.”
22. “He called upon his Lord: 'These are a criminal people.'”
23. “'Lead My servants forth by night. Surely you will be pursued.'”
24. “'Leave the sea as a dry path. Surely they are a host that will be overtaken.'”
25. “How many gardens and springs they left behind.”
26. “How many crops and noble places.”
27. “How many blessings in which they lived at ease.”
28. “Thus We made another people heirs to them.”
29. “The heaven and the earth did not weep for them; nor were they given respite.”
30. “We delivered the Children of Israel from the abasing punishment.”
31. “From Pharaoh. Surely he was a headstrong criminal.”
32. “We chose them above the worlds upon a knowledge.”
33. “We gave them such signs as in which was a clear trial.”
Etymological-Semantic Analysis:
“Rasulun karim”: the root K-R-M means “precious, honorable, generous.” Zeccac explains “karim” as “one in whom worth and virtue are gathered.” Moses' attribute of “karim” stresses the nobility of the message and the honor of the envoy. Pharaoh, however, weighs the message not by its content but by status; the attribute “karim” reverses this evaluation by status: true worth lies not in power but in the nobility of the message.
“Tariqan yebasa”: Y-B-S means “dry, hard, the water withdrawn.” Zeccac defines “yebes” as “terrain from which the water has withdrawn and hardened.” The symbolic counterpart: stability (dry ground) taking the place of uncertainty (water/sea). Order taking the place of chaos, security the place of fear. The rational counterpart: the passage from the environment of uncertainty the system of oppression created to the environment of security the system of justice creates.
“Mustakbirun”: from the root K-B-R, “to grow great, to hold oneself superior.” Pharaoh's claim “I am your Lord most high” is the historical archetype of the principle of “power and deviation” in article 1a of the Protocol. Power inevitably produces inequality; religion was sent to break this presupposition.
“Ma taraku”: “what they left.” This expression denotes the material accumulation that remained after the collapse of the system of oppression (gardens, springs, crops, places). Zeccac explains “taraku” as “to leave behind, to forsake.” The semantic message: wealth accumulated through oppression loses its meaning with the death of the oppressor; for that wealth was built not upon justice but upon exploitation.
Rational Analysis:
The Pharaoh paradigm is, beyond a historical event, the archetype of the intoxication of power of all times. The rational core is this:
1. The poisoning of power: Pharaoh, saying “give me Allah's servants,” regards human beings as property. This is the inevitable consequence of the absolutizing of power.
2. The collapse of the system: the expression “leave the sea as a dry path” represents the passage from the environment of uncertainty the system of oppression created to the ground of justice. The host of Pharaoh's being “a host that will be overtaken” is the proclamation that the system of oppression will collapse through its own contradictions.
3. The transfer of the inheritance: the expression “We made another people heirs” expresses the passage, after the collapse of the system of oppression, to the system of justice. This is the Sunnatullah principle of article 1f of the Protocol: destruction is not “a sudden execution” but a systemic collapse.
4. “The heaven and the earth did not weep for them”: this expression tells of the incompatibility of the system of oppression with the cosmic order. An unjust system contradicts the universal order (the Mizan); when it collapses, the universe does not “weep” for it — that is, its absence is lived not as a loss but as a correction.
As required by article 20a of the Protocol (tanZih), the expressions of “Allah's taking vengeance” or “the heaven's weeping” cannot be read as the ascribing of human feelings to Allah. These are the symbolic tellings of the operating of the universal law of justice.
Structural Sociology:
The Pharaonic system is the historical example of the principle “the form changed, the essence did not” in article 1e of the Protocol. The relation of the landowner and the peasant takes concrete form in the relation of Pharaoh and the Children of Israel. Today this relation has become the relation of the owners of capital, who hold the means of production, and the wage laborer.
The expression “how many gardens and springs they left” shows the unsustainability of wealth accumulated through oppression. The zakat principle of article 11 of the Protocol, keeping wealth in circulation, prevents the formation of this kind of accumulation (and therewith of the system of oppression).
The expression “We chose the Children of Israel above the worlds” is not an ethnic superiority but a historical assignment of responsibility. The expression “a clear trial” stresses that this choosing is not a privilege but a test.
Maqasid Detail:
The maqsad of this group is to show, through a historical archetype, the inevitable collapse of the system of oppression. The aim is not to give the Meccan aristocracy the message “you too will collapse like Pharaoh,” but to recall a universal law (Sunnatullah): oppression is not sustainable; justice will sooner or later be manifest.
THE FOURTH GROUP: AD-DUKHAN 34-42 — THE SMOKE (DUKHAN) AND THE DENIAL OF THE RESURRECTION
The Translation (el-Kashshaf):
34. “Surely these are saying:”
35. “'There is no death but our first death. We shall not be raised.'”
36. “'Bring our fathers, if you speak the truth.'”
37. “Are these better, or the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them. Surely they were criminals.”
38. “We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.”
39. “We created them only with truth. But most of them do not know.”
40. “Surely the day of separation is the time when they shall all be gathered.”
41. “On that day no friend shall avail a friend, and they shall not be helped.”
42. “Except those upon whom Allah has had mercy. Surely He is the Mighty, the Merciful.”
Etymological-Semantic Analysis:
“Al-mawtatatu'l-ula”: “the first death.” The root M-W-T means “death, the ending of life.” “Ula” means “first.” The rational counterpart: biological death in this world. The deniers' claim is this: “We die once, and there is nothing after.” This claim removes the consciousness of responsibility (taqwa); for if there is no reckoning, the demand for justice also becomes meaningless.
“La'b”: “play.” The root L-'-B is the same root as the “yal'abun” of verse 9. The expression “We did not create the heavens and the earth in play” proclaims that the universe carries a purpose, that it is not a meaningless chaos. The rational counterpart: the universe is teleological (purposeful); human life likewise is not a meaningless game but a process bearing responsibility.
“Yawmu'l-fasl”: F-S-L means “to separate, to give a definitive judgment.” “The day of separation” expresses the day on which right will be separated from falsehood, justice from oppression, the straight from the crooked, definitively. The rational counterpart: the moment at which the consequences of actions appear in full, when no ambiguity remains.
“Mawla”: the root W-L-Y means “friend, protector, possessor.” The expression “no friend shall avail a friend” expresses that worldly relations (ties of blood, class solidarity, political alliance) will lose their validity on that day. The rational counterpart: responsibility is individual; no social belonging can transfer a person's reckoning to another.
Rational Analysis:
The rational core of this group is to expose the psychology behind the denial of the resurrection. The claim “there is no death but our first death” in truth means “I do not want to give account.” For if there is resurrection and reckoning, oppression is not sustainable; justice will sooner or later be manifest.
The expression “We did not create the heavens and the earth in play” rejects the materialist and nihilist worldview. The universe is not “an amusement park” but a field of responsibility. This is connected with the liberty principle of article 1b of the Protocol: liberty without responsibility is meaningless; responsibility without reckoning is meaningless.
The reference to “the people of Tubba'” is a historical warning: there were powerful peoples before you; they too were criminals and were destroyed. This shows the historical continuity of Sunnatullah (the universal law).
Structural Sociology:
The expression “no friend shall avail a friend” proclaims that tribal solidarity (asabiyya) will lose its validity on that day. In jahiliyya society the individual existed through his tribe; the tribal chief assumed the individual's reckoning. The revelation breaks this structure: responsibility is individual; no social belonging can take over the individual's reckoning before Allah. This is the individual dimension of the structural sociological revolution of article 29 of the Protocol.

text:
I would not write if I did not read the Histories by Herodotus. 

Regarding your post, the following questions could be asked, namely: 
(1) Whether the inflammatory speech, insidious propaganda and incitement to crime preceded the criminal offence? 
(2) Whether the acts of communication that feed on, disseminate and actively intensify pre-existing bias if not hatred towards an education, religion, ancestors, honesty represent a precursor to as well as a catalyst for the committed criminal offence? 
(3) Whether widespread and repeated instances of hate speech may amount to acts precursory to or preparatory of a criminal offence in that they increase the general risk of this criminal offence? 
(4) Whether the crime of incitement consists of an unlawful communication by the inciter to the incitee, made with the intent to move, influence, encourage or prompt the incitee towards the commission of crime? (5) Whether the proof of a causal link between the act of incitement and an unlawful result is not required? (6) Whether the crime is committed even though the incitee remains unresponsive to the inciter’s efforts to move him towards the commission of crime? 
(7) Whether the accused reached and sought to influence the mind of the other person towards the commission of a crime? 
(8) Whether the crime of incitement is essentially premised on the inciter’s guilty mind accompanied by conduct in the form of some effective act of communication directed to the incitee? 
(9) Whether incitement cannot be committed negligently? 
(10) Whether the form of intent on the part of the accused, dolus eventualis may suffice, that is, it can be shown that the accused foresaw the possibility that her communication would reach and influence the mind of the incitee but proceeded anyway? 
(11) Whether any person who incites, instigates, commands, or procures any other person to commit any offence, either at common law or against a statute or statutory regulation, may be guilty of an offence? 
(12) Whether the principle nullum crimen sine lege may be invoked to preclude any prosecutorial efforts based on joint reading of the national act which cannot serve as a basis for the prosecution of a crime in question and the International act? 
(13) Whether the crime of genocide does not require the successful destruction in whole or in part of an ethnic group or another group protected by Article II of the Genocide Convention? 
(14) Whether the crime of genocide requires the intent to destroy a protected group and the actus reus of the offence does not require the actual destruction of the group? 
(15) Whether all crimes of genocide are better characterised as attempt to commit genocide? 
(16) Whether what can be attempted in relation to genocide is the underlying offence, that is, killing, causing serious bodily or mental harm, etc.? 
(17) Whether a person can be guilty of an attempt to commit a crime if he, inter alia, acted with the kind of culpability otherwise required for commission of the crime? 
(18) Whether a person can be guilty of an attempt to commit a crime if he purposely engaged in conduct that would constitute the crime if the attendant circumstances were as he believed them to be? 
(19) Whether a person can be guilty of an attempt to commit a crime if he did or omitted to do anything with the purpose of causing or with the belief that it would cause such a result without further conduct on his part? 
(20) Whether a person can be guilty of an attempt to commit a crime if he purposely did or omitted to do anything that, under the circumstances as he believed them to be, were an act or omission constituting a substantial step in a course of conduct planned to culminate in his commission of the crime? 
(21) Whether the intent can be defined as the person’s means to engage in the conduct? 
(22) Whether the intent can be defined as the person’s means to cause the consequence? 
(23) Whether the intent can be defined as the person’s awareness that the consequence will occur in the ordinary course of events? 
(24) Whether the crime of aggression criminalizes individuals for their contributions to state aggression? (25) Whether it can be determined without a reasonable doubt who is to be held accountable for aggression? 
(26) Whether there is a clear consensus among international lawyers that only leaders ought to be blamed for aggression? 
(27) Whether it is generally accepted that only high-ranking state agents can be held responsible for the crime of aggression, whereas common foot soldiers and followers ought to be excluded from criminal responsibility? 
(28) Whether according to the Article 8bis of the Statute of the International Criminal Court (Rome Statute) the crime of aggression is defined as follows: “For the purpose of this Statute, ‘crime of aggression’ means the planning, preparation, initiation or execution, by a person in a position effectively to exercise control over or to direct the political or military action of a State, of an act of aggression which, by its character, gravity and scale, constitutes a manifest violation of the Charter of the United Nations”? 
(29) Whether the essence of individual criminal responsibility is the appraisal of individual contribution against the requirements imposed by the basic structure of international crimes? 
(30) Whether, pursuant to the Rome Statute, international crimes consist of material (actus reus/objective) and mental (mens rea/subjective) elements? 
(31) Whether in order to establish guilt, the court has to make objective and subjective links between the accused and the offence in question? 
(32) Whether the objective aspect (that is, actus reus) is broken down into conduct, consequence and circumstance? 
(33) Whether the subjective aspect (that is, mens rea) consists of intent and knowledge? 
(34) Whether it is the collective act that bedevils the crime of aggression and complicates individual criminal responsibility? 
(35) Whether the collective act (intrinsic to the crime of aggression) is a consequence or a circumstance element? 
(36) Whether the distinction among material elements is crucial because different mental elements apply to conduct, consequence and circumstance? 
(37) Whether the distinction among material elements is crucial because, as a rule, individuals are blamed for the caused wrong that is manifested in the consequence element of the crime? 
(38) Whether the individuals are not blamed for the surrounding circumstances in which the criminal act took place? 
(39) Whether circumstances exist irrespective of the perpetrator’s conduct? 
(40) Whether the leadership clause referred to in Article 25 of the Rome Statute, which stipulates that the article’s provision on modes of criminal responsibility applies only to a person who meets the requirements of this clause, requires that a perpetrator “control or direct” “state action”? 
(41) Whether the state action (collective act) could be interpreted as either a consequence or a circumstance element or both? 
(42) Whether the mental elements of a crime presuppose a required state of mind (intent and knowledge), viz. the psychological relationship between the offender and the offence? 
(43) Whether Article 30 of the Rome Statute prescribes the necessary mental elements and is seen as a general provision in international criminal law? (44) Whether, as a rule, in order to be blamed for the international crime, the person has to voluntarily engage in the conduct, be aware of all required circumstances prescribed by the specific crime, and be virtually certain that the consequences will occur? 
(45) Whether material elements determine did the individual act wrongfully? 
(46) Whether wrongfulness is a breach of a prohibitory norm, that is, a norm that prohibits criminal conduct? (47) Whether, stricto senso, actus reus is the conduct that denotes an action or omission that is contained in the definition of a specific crime? 
(48) Whether “conduct” is an action or omission and its accompanying state of mind, or, where relevant, a series of acts and omissions? 
(49) Whether, for example, an action could be “planning” of the crime of aggression; an example of omission is starvation of civilians as a method of warfare in armed conflict? 
(50) Whether an action always renders a change in the material world (e.g. firing of a pistol)? 
(51) Whether an omission is non-performance of an action in instances where there is a legal duty to perform? 
(52) Whether Element 1 and Article 8bis of the Rome Statute define the conduct of the crime of aggression as planning, preparation, initiation or execution of an act of aggression? 
(53) Whether one does not wage an act of aggression but rather executes it? 
(54) Whether, for the purpose of the Rome Statute, a person commits a “crime of aggression” when, being in a position effectively to exercise control over or to direct the political or military action of a State, that person intentionally and knowingly orders or participates actively in the planning, preparation, initiation or execution of an act of aggression which, by its character, gravity and scale, constitutes a flagrant violation of the Charter of the United Nations? 
(55) Whether the literal definition of planning is “to arrange in advance (an action or proposed proceeding)”, “to devise, contrive, or formulate (a project or manner of proceeding)”, “to lay out a plan”? 
(56) Whether, accordingly, one’s participation in devising a plan is what is criminalized? 
(57) Whether the term “plan” is defined as “an organised (and usually detailed) proposal according to which something is to be done? 
(58) Whether the above means that the perpetrator has to be physically present and give his input during the crucial meetings where the plan for the specific act of aggression is devised? 
(59) Whether criminalization reaches as far as the development of specified plans and operations towards the commission of the particular state action in question? 
(60) Whether preparation has a similar meaning as planning? 
(61) Whether ILC in its Nuremberg judgement held that “the terms “planning” and “preparation” of a war of aggression were considered by the Tribunal as comprising all the stages in the bringing about of a war of aggression from the planning to the actual initiation of the war? 
(62) Whether, if planning denotes participation in devising a proposal for action, preparation refers to subsequent and sometimes simultaneous acts of creating conditions that enable such action? 
(63) Whether the following can be the examples for preparation: creating a public option of the necessity of war through the mainstream media, acquiring weapons, recruiting troops and getting them ready for warfare, and so on? 
(64) Whether initiation denotes the commencement of the use of force required by the definition of the crime of aggression? 
(65) Whether at the Nuremberg Military Tribunal, initiation was described as “... a unilateral operation?
(66) When war is formally declared or the first shot is fired the initiation of the war has ended and from then on there is a waging of war between the two adversaries”? 
(67) Whether the term initiation captures actions on the strategic level pertaining to decisions directly leading to the use of force, as opposed to decisions to act aggressively (planning stage) and decisions at the tactical level that are subsequent to initiation of the state action? 
(68) Whether execution present in the Element 1 and Article 8bis of the Rome Statute replaced Nuremberg’s “waging”, and there is no case law or any clarification from the Special Working Group for the Crime of Aggression (SWGCA) regarding this element? 
(69) Whether according to the dictionary, the term “execution” denotes “the action of carrying into effect (a plan, design, purpose, command, decree, task, etc.)”? 
(70) Whether the execution stage is subsequent to initiation and therefore encompasses all further actions in furtherance of aggression? 
(71) Whether execution is confined to contributions of individuals of greater importance? 
(72) Whether the above argument is in line with the basic premise of the leadership requirement, that is, the crime of aggression is a leadership crime that excludes followers from criminal responsibility? 
(73) Whether in order for a synchronized collective action to occur, a proposal of some kind must first be made? 
(74) Whether preparations for the execution of such a plan have to follow logically? 
(75) Whether as a third step, strategic decisions have to be made to narrow down the object that will be absorbed by the action? 
(76) Whether, finally, in a collective endeavour, someone has to order the beginning of the course of action? 
(77) Whether the ultimate product or the result of such a collective endeavour is a challenge in the natural world---in this case the use of violence (in the case of Inchoate offence criminal conspiracy it could be the use of falsified documents, false statements)? 
(78) Whether in light of the foregoing, conduct can be read as being a contribution to one of the stages prior to the consequence of the crime? 
(79) Whether is it true that, whenever there is an element of collectiveness implied in the commission of a certain act, there are at least two stages prior to action, viz. planning and execution of an act? 
(80) Whether, according to the current doctrine at the ICC, the person in control over the commission of the crime is responsible for the offence as the perpetrator? 
(81) Whether “control” can be exerted not only by those who “physically carry out the objective elements of the offence but also by those who, in spite of being removed from the scene of the crime, mastermind its commission because they decide whether and how the offence will be committed”? 
(82) Whether the ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I defined the “control” required for perpetration as an essential contribution to the commission of the crime?

FMINO PRESS RELEASE

AFRICAN MINISTERS MOVE TO ESTABLISH COMMON COMMUNICATION FRONT, REVIVE ANNUAL CONTINENTAL MEETINGS

African Ministers of Information have called for a coordinated continental communication framework to combat misinformation, strengthen public trust and project Africa's voice globally. The call emerged from a high-level roundtable on responsible communication at the World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) on Wednesday, in Abuja, where participants proposed stronger institutional cooperation, professional capacity building and regular consultations among African governments.

The Honourable Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, said the proliferation of digital platforms and artificial intelligence had made credible and responsible communication a strategic governance priority. Citing Nigeria's experience with manipulated videos and misinformation, he warned that false narratives could distort public events, create panic and undermine confidence in government.

“Technology has come to stay. AI is here to help us if we use it properly. The challenge is to ensure that what we communicate is credible and honest,” Idris said.

The Minister stressed the need to restore sustained cooperation among African information managers, recalling that the continent previously maintained platforms for collective engagement. He proposed reviving the Annual Conference of African Ministers of Information to strengthen policy coordination and enable Africa to speak with a common voice on issues of shared interest.

“Collectively, we are stronger if we are united. There is a need to establish a robust system that enables us to look at Africa as one and speak with one voice once again,” he stated.

Idris also urged African countries to support Nigeria's UNESCO Category 2 International Media and Information Literacy Institute in Abuja and strengthen collaboration among public media institutions, including NTA, FRCN, NAN and VON, to promote content exchange and African narratives.

“The Media and Information Literacy Institute is not just a Nigerian institution; it is a global opportunity. We should support it as part of a broader continental effort to promote media literacy, particularly among our young people,” he said.

Kenya's Cabinet Secretary for Information, Communications and Digital Economy, H.E. Hon. William Kabogo Gitau, EGH, highlighted Kenya's National Communication Policy, adopted in August 2026, and plans for a National Communication Centre to provide verified government information and facilitate citizen feedback. He also advocated professional regulation of public relations and stronger cross-border cooperation against misinformation.

“Trust between a state and its citizens is built through ordinary interactions: a question answered accurately, a service delivered as promised, and the same message from every part of the country. One government, one message, consistent,” Kabogo said.

The Minister of Communication and Media and Government Spokesperson of the Republic of the Congo (Congo-Brazzaville), Thierry Lézin Moungalla, called for a continental framework for ministerial consultations, professional training, public-private media partnerships and joint content production. He emphasised that government communication must be integrated into the strategic machinery of governance.

“Government communication is no longer simply a public relations function. It must be strategic and structural, embedded in the framework of government administration,” Moungalla stated.

The Deputy Minister of Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services of Zimbabwe, Hon. Dr. Omphile Marupi, highlighted Zimbabwe's 16 community radio stations and grassroots information structures as tools for inclusive communication. He called for stronger media literacy, ethical journalism and African ownership of the continent's narratives.

“We must communicate not simply to be heard, but to be understood. We must not only disseminate information, but also listen, engage and respond to the concerns of our people,” Marupi said.

The Chairman of the Information and Communications Committee of the Parliament of Ghana and Member of Parliament for Bunkpurugu Constituency, Hon. Dr. Abed-Nego Lamangin Bandim, advocated increased investment in government communication, expanded rural connectivity and improved welfare for journalists. He disclosed that Ghana had earmarked 10 million Ghana cedis in its 2027 budget for journalists' training, development and welfare.

“We cannot succeed with inadequate budgetary allocations for government communication. We must also ensure that journalists are properly supported and remunerated if we expect them to produce credible and independent information for our people,” Bandim said.

The roundtable ended with a shared commitment to strengthen continental communication cooperation, with Nigeria indicating its readiness to host the next meeting of African Ministers of Information.

Rabiu Ibrahim, mnipr 
Special Assistant (Media) to the Honourable Minister of Information and National Orientation

19 November, 2026

Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, NI (M), HJ, Chief of Army Staff, & Chief of Defence Forces (COAS & CDF), visited Turbat, Balochistan. Upon arrival the Field Marshal laid a floral wreath at the Shuhada Monument and offered Fateha. 

The Field Marshal was given a comprehensive briefing on the prevailing security environment, operational preparedness and successful on-going operations against externally sponsored terrorism. He was also apprised of the progress of various ongoing socio-economic development initiatives for people of Balochistan.

During interaction with troops, the Field Marshal commended their high state of operational preparedness, professionalism and unwavering resolve to defend the motherland, amidst challenging operational conditions. 

Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir reaffirmed Pakistan Army’s unwavering commitment to stand shoulder to shoulder with the people of Balochistan in their continued pursuit of peace, prosperity and sustainable development. 

Upon arrival, the Field Marshal was received by Corps Commander Balochistan.

text:
HUNGER CRISIS GRIPS MAKERERE UNIVERSITY AS STUDENTS COLLAPSE DURING EXAMS AMID RISING COSTS.

A deepening hunger crisis at Uganda’s premier institution, Makerere University, has left students skipping meals, missing examinations, collapsing from exhaustion, and in some cases requiring hospitalisation as the examination period unfolds in November 2026. Reports circulating on social media and in local outlets describe students struggling to concentrate, losing weight, and developing health complications simply because they cannot afford regular food. One widely shared post claimed students were “dying of hunger” and collapsing in exam halls, highlighting a stark contrast with statements made by Vice Chancellor Prof Barnabas Nawangwe roughly two years earlier, when university officials publicly denied that any students were going hungry.

The immediate trigger for institutional action was mounting evidence that hunger was directly interfering with academic performance. On 11 November 2026, Makerere University partnered with the Rotary Club of Makerere Passport to launch the Food for Peace programme. The initiative initially targets 206 students identified through a needs assessment conducted by the Makerere Rotary Peace Centre. These students, drawn from both government- and privately sponsored ranks, receive free meals at participating halls of residence during the examination period so they can sit papers without an empty stomach. Prof Nawangwe, who also serves as president of the Rotary club, openly acknowledged the severity of the situation, stating that the university had “noticed some being taken by ambulance to hospital just because of hunger.” He framed the programme as a temporary but necessary intervention to protect academic integrity while longer-term solutions are sought.

At the heart of the crisis is the inadequacy of financial support relative to living costs in Kampala. Government-sponsored students receive a living/meal allowance of approximately USh 530,000 per semester. Spread across a typical 120-day semester, this equates to roughly USh 4,400 per day. A single modest meal near campus—rice, chapati, chips and beans—can cost around USh 3,500, while protein options such as offals (USh 4,000), stewed beef (USh 5,000), chicken (USh 8,000) or fish (USh 10,000) quickly exhaust the daily allocation. Many students therefore rely on cheap street food such as plain chapati, Rolex or cassava, or simply skip meals altogether. Privately sponsored students, whose families have already stretched resources to cover tuition and rent, face similar or greater pressures when home remittances are irregular or insufficient.

Student leaders have been vocal. Guild President Gracious Kadondi, herself a government-sponsored student, noted that the allowance arrives at the beginning of the semester and is often exhausted by examination time. Innocent Kisembo, chairperson of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, described the USh 530,000 figure as “too little to push someone for the entire semester.” Third-year student Denise Kainomugisha told reporters she routinely attends lectures on an empty stomach and returns to her hostel hoping she has both food supplies and cooking gas. She observed that without a side hustle or consistent parental support, many students simply “get used to not eating the whole day.”

This is not an entirely new problem. In 2018 the university discontinued direct meal provision in halls after caterers demanded higher payments amid rising commodity prices and switched to cash allowances following a student survey. In late 2024, delayed disbursement of those allowances sparked protests by government-sponsored students. University officials at the time dismissed some starvation claims as inaccurate, and several student leaders were briefly suspended before the suspensions were lifted. Those earlier episodes, combined with the current reports of hospitalisations and missed exams, have prompted renewed scrutiny. Parliamentary attention has also been drawn; Deputy Speaker Thomas Tayebwa directed the Committee on Education and Sports to examine student living allowances.

The Food for Peace programme offers immediate relief for a few hundred students, and Rotary International Director Emmanuel Katongole has pledged annual support. Yet student leaders and commentators argue that 206 beneficiaries represent only a fraction of those affected at a university with tens of thousands of students. They call for a permanent student food bank, an emergency welfare fund, and a review of allowance levels and disbursement timing so that support lasts through examinations. Prof Nawangwe has also warned that food insecurity can expose vulnerable students, particularly young women, to exploitation.

For now, the contrast remains striking: an institution that once denied the existence of hungry students is now publicly feeding starving candidates so they can finish their examinations. Whether the current emergency response evolves into sustained welfare reform will determine how many future Makerere students can focus on their studies rather than their next meal.

🇨🇳 | 🇺🇸 🇷🇺 | The Trump–Putin bilateral meeting in Shenzhen, ahead of their subsequent encounter with Xi Jinping, may be less about securing an immediate agreement than about establishing the political parameters of their engagement. For Trump, the exchange offers an opportunity to demonstrate that Washington and Moscow can negotiate directly, explore potential diplomatic openings and establish a channel that does not depend on Beijing. For Putin, it provides international visibility, reinforces Russia's status as a major power and allows him to test Trump's willingness to pursue a negotiated approach to Ukraine, sanctions and strategic stability.

Ukraine is likely to remain the most sensitive underlying issue, even if no concrete settlement is discussed. The two presidents may seek to gauge the scope of possible negotiations, the conditions for a ceasefire and the political limits of any concessions, without confusing preliminary discussions with an actual agreement. Nuclear arms control and broader security questions could also offer common ground, particularly as Washington seeks to address China's expanding strategic capabilities.

The bilateral also carries a message for Xi. Trump wants to demonstrate that he can engage both Moscow and Beijing independently, while Putin has an interest in maintaining his partnership with China without becoming entirely dependent on it. Xi, meanwhile, has an opportunity to position China as the indispensable diplomatic centre of the encounter, shaping the broader conversation without necessarily committing to outcomes that conflict with Beijing's interests.

The significance of Shenzhen may therefore lie less in what the three leaders formally agree to than in what they establish privately about the limits of cooperation, the issues they are prepared to negotiate and the balance of leverage each brings to the table. The bilateral sets the tone; the trilateral tests whether their overlapping interests can translate into a broader diplomatic understanding — or whether their strategic differences remain too deep to bridge.

text:
Another way to quickly find clients in the US or Europe. I have tested this method myself. It works specifically for small local businesses: restaurants, laundromats, service contractors, and anyone listed on Google Maps.

I didn't invent this approach. Below is an almost word-for-word breakdown of a real Reddit case study that describes the process accurately.

For two months, the author sent cold emails to local service companies (HVAC, contractors) and got a 1% reply rate. He tested subject lines, calls to action, and send times. Nothing changed.

The problem was at step one: he was scraping Google Maps and emailing generic info@ addresses. The owner of a three-person company doesn't sit in the general inbox. Once he switched to finding verified direct contacts for decision-makers, his reply rate jumped from 1% to 4-8%.

Here is the step-by-step workflow:

1. Scrape Google Maps. Search by niche and city. Use a simple filter: at least 10 reviews and a working website to filter out dead listings right away. One search usually yields 50-80 companies.

2. Check the website. Look for three things: whether the site is active, if the owner's name is listed anywhere (About page, footer, team page), and what corporate email format they use.

3. Find the owner if the site doesn't list them. Spend 2-3 minutes checking four sources: a Google search for "[company name] owner", industry directories and the Better Business Bureau, the company's LinkedIn page (in small businesses, the owner is often the only person listed), and public business registries. If nothing turns up in a couple of minutes, move on.

4. Guess and verify the email. Build standard patterns from the name (first@domain, firstname.lastname@domain, etc.) and run them through SMTP verifiers like NeverBounce or Bouncer. Don't skip this. One unverified send gave the author a 14% bounce rate and burned his domain reputation.

5. Personalize using reviews. Google Maps reviews are a goldmine. Customers mention response times, pricing, or specific technicians by name. A single line referencing a real detail from a review outperforms any generic icebreaker.

6. Clean the spreadsheet and send via Instantly to keep deliverability under control.

Manually, this whole cycle takes 5-6 hours per 100 contacts. With a stack like WebLeads or Outscraper plus Instantly, it drops to 20 minutes, leaving only personalization to be done by hand.

What matters in practice:

You can do all of this manually with zero tech stack. Or you can set up scripts and AI tools to run it semi-automatically or fully automatically.

Either way, it still comes down to three things:

1. The offer: what you actually write in that first email to make someone want to reply.
2. Segmentation: picking the exact companies that genuinely need what you are offering.
3. English: first comes the email thread, then the call. You either handle it yourself or put someone with solid spoken English on that step.

One important note from my own experience. When I sent emails to generic info@domain addresses myself, my reply rate reached 3%. So the problem isn't always the inbox. It all comes down to how you frame your offer.

A marketer who can show a real case study and make a strong promise is almost always in demand. For a business owner, marketing is always a direct question of how their revenue is going to change.

text:
In a small Bronx hospital ward in the 1940s, a woman named Bessie Blount moved quietly between rows of beds — not just doing her job, but refusing to accept the limits everyone else had already decided were permanent.
Her patients were young men. World War II veterans who had come home alive — but barely. Men who had lost arms, hands, and the ability to do the things most of us never think twice about. Things like lifting a fork. Like eating a meal on their own. Like feeling, even for ten minutes a day, that they were still the men they had been before the war took pieces of them.
Bessie was their physical therapist. And she was relentless.
She taught veterans who had lost their arms how to write again — using their feet, their teeth, whatever still worked. She had learned those same techniques herself as a child, after a schoolteacher punished her for writing with her left hand. Rather than surrender, young Bessie had taught herself to write with both hands, and then with her teeth, and then with her toes. She turned a punishment into a superpower — and decades later, she used that superpower to give others their independence back.
But one day, a doctor said something that stopped her in her tracks.
What these men really needed, he said, was a way to feed themselves.
Bessie heard that and went home. She turned her apartment into a laboratory. She spent five years and three thousand dollars of her own money — money she didn't have to spare — testing, redesigning, and rebuilding, night after night, until she had something that worked.
The device was elegantly simple. A tube. A spoon-shaped mouthpiece. A bite-activated switch. When a patient bit down, the machine delivered a single mouthful of food. When they were ready for more, they bit down again. No hands required. No help needed. A veteran who had lost both arms could sit down to a meal and eat every bite of it completely on his own — with full control, full dignity, and nobody having to do it for him.
She filed for a patent in 1948. It was granted in April 1951.
Then she brought it to the United States government. The Veterans Administration looked at it, considered it, and said no.
No explanation grand enough to justify the rejection. No counter-offer. Just — no.
Bessie could have stopped there. Most people would have. But she wasn't most people.
In 1952, she boarded a plane to France and handed over the rights to her invention — freely, deliberately, and with a purpose that had nothing to do with money. The French government immediately recognized its value and moved to put it into production for their disabled veterans. When asked years later why she had given it away rather than fight for compensation, she was clear: it was never about the money. It was about proving, to anyone watching, that a Black woman could invent something that changed the world.
America had turned her away. She made sure the world didn't forget what they passed on.
But Bessie Blount Griffin didn't define herself by one invention, or even one career.
In the years that followed, she reinvented herself entirely. She began studying handwriting — not as a hobby, but as a science. She noticed that the way people wrote revealed something about their health, their stress, their state of mind. She published a technical paper on what she called """"""""medical graphology."""""""" Law enforcement agencies took notice. She became the chief document examiner for a Virginia police department, helping solve cases of fraud, embezzlement, and forgery.
Then, in 1977, at the age of 63 — when most people are thinking about slowing down — Bessie received an invitation from Scotland Yard in London to join their advanced studies program in their Document Division. She accepted. She became the first Black woman ever accepted into that program, earning the affectionate nickname """"""""Mama Bessie"""""""" from colleagues who quickly understood they were in the presence of someone rare.
She returned to the United States and ran her own forensic consulting business well into her eighties. She authenticated documents related to slavery, the Civil War, and Native American treaties. She testified in courtrooms. She kept solving problems that other people had decided weren't worth solving.
Bessie Blount Griffin died in 2009 at the age of 95.
She never became a household name. She never had a movie made about her life. But somewhere in the long history of assistive technology — the devices that help people eat, communicate, and live with independence — her hands are in the foundation.
She didn't wait for permission. She didn't wait for recognition. She didn't wait for America to change its mind.
She just got to work.
And the world is better — quietly, profoundly, undeniably better — because she did.

Some people spend their whole lives waiting to be chosen. Bessie Blount Griffin spent hers proving she already was

GOVERNMENT OF ZIMBABWE THROUGH PRESIDENT MNANGAGWA COMMENDED FOR REWARDING SPORTING EXCELLENCE. 

The recent recognition and rewarding of Zimbabwean athletes by the Government through President Emmerson Mnangagwa—most notably honoring 17-year-old Youth Olympic 200m gold medalist Ropafadzo Liberty Mzondo and the senior national football team, the Warriors, at State House, alongside earlier vehicle and cash awards to rugby, boxing, and domestic football stars—highlights a deliberate push to elevate the status of sport in Zimbabwe.   

Why the Commendation is Merited

Tangible Motivation for Athletes: For decades, many Zimbabwean sportspersons competed with minimal financial return, often relying on personal sacrifice to represent the country. Direct presidential recognition, cash incentives, and vehicles provide immediate, life-changing motivation and show that national pride is backed by concrete appreciation.   

Inspiration for Youth and Grassroots Talent: Honoring young trailblazers like Mzondo sends a clear signal to school-level and emerging athletes that sporting excellence is a viable, respected path to national honor and economic empowerment.

Cross-Discipline Inclusion: Extending rewards across football, rugby, track and field, women's sport, and Special Olympics teams demonstrates a broader commitment beyond just one mainstream discipline.   

Nation Branding and Sports Tourism: Celebrating international victories strengthens national unity and positions Zimbabwe positively on the global stage.

The commendation reflects genuine gratitude from the sporting fraternity for high-level recognition that boosts morale, while serving as a reminder that pairing rewards with long-term sports development will yield the greatest dividends for Zimbabwean sport.

We will continue to nurture and develop sporting talent, says President

President Dr @edmnangagwa has reaffirmed Government's commitment to nurturing and developing sporting talent across the country, saying no community will be left behind as Zimbabwe strengthens its sports development structures from grassroots level to international competition.

Speaking at a reception held at State House yesterday in honour of the Warriors following their 3-0 victory over Equatorial Guinea and Youth Olympic gold medallist Ropafadzo Liberty Mzondo, President Mnangagwa said Government would continue investing in systems that identify, nurture and develop athletes from schools and communities through to international competition.

He described the Warriors' victory and Mzondo's historic Youth Olympic gold medal as defining achievements that reflect the resilience, talent and potential of Zimbabweans.

President Mnangagwa congratulated the Warriors, coach Ramon Catala and the technical team for their commanding performance, saying the win demonstrated teamwork, tactical discipline, determination and unity. He urged the squad to maintain its momentum and secure qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

The President also commended football supporters who braved rainy conditions to rally behind the national team, saying the return of international football to the National Sports Stadium had reignited the nation's passion for the game.

He said the Warriors' triumph, together with the Sables' recent rugby victory over Namibia, highlighted the importance of investing in world class sporting infrastructure and pledged to accelerate the upgrading and maintenance of sports facilities nationwide.

President Mnangagwa challenged local authorities, the private sector and sports administrators to play a greater role in developing and maintaining sporting and recreational facilities, while strengthening grassroots sport, talent identification, athlete development, coaching and sports administration.

Turning to Mzondo, President Mnangagwa hailed the 17-year-old sprinter's Youth Olympic gold medal as a national achievement that had placed Zimbabwe firmly on the global sporting map.

He encouraged the youngster to continue representing the country with distinction at the forthcoming African Union Sports Council Region 5 Games in Maputo, Mozambique, adding that his success should inspire other young Zimbabweans to pursue their dreams with discipline, hard work and determination.

The reception was attended by Sport, Recreation, Arts and Culture Minister Lt-Gen (Rtd) Anselem Nhamo Sanyatwe, Harare Metropolitan Provincial Affairs and Devolution Minister Cde Charles Tawengwa, Chief Secretary to the President and Cabinet Dr Martin Rushwaya, ZIFA president Nqobile Magwizi, legislators, former players, Zimbabwe Olympic Committee officials and development partners.

Brood parasitism, also called nest parasitism, is originally the behavior of certain bird species that lay their eggs in the nests of other individuals, of the same species or not, thereby benefiting from the food intended for the entire brood. The host pair incubates the intruder egg and feeds the chick until it reaches maturity. It is a particular form of kleptoparasitism. The best-known example is the common cuckoo, which parasitizes the nests of various passerine species. Similar behavior, also called brood parasitism, has developed in other animal groups: salamanders, fish, and insects. (...) Laying an egg in the nest of another bird species without being noticed and having the intruder offspring raised by its false parents until maturity is not straightforward. A variety of adaptations have developed in parasitic species to succeed in their maneuver. Females are very discreet when approaching a host’s nest to lay an egg. Some parasitic species closely monitor the activity of several potential hosts at once in order to know the best moment to act without being detected. In several cuckoo species, the male sometimes intentionally distracts the hosts by singing near the nest in order to give the female an opportunity while he is being aggressively pursued by them. Some parasites destroy an egg from the brood that they replace with their own, perhaps to prevent the hosts from noticing the subterfuge by finding one extra egg in the nest. In the parasite, egg-laying is very rapid. The great spotted cuckoo can lay an egg in two or three seconds, whereas on average a bird requires several minutes to lay an egg. The development of the chicks of parasitic species is also very rapid. It grows faster than the host’s young and, being larger and more robust, monopolizes the food brought by the host adults. At the moment of hatching, young honeyguides are equipped with small teeth at the tips of their mandibles. Still naked and blind, they wound and kill the other chicks with these teeth. The dead chicks are then removed from the nest by the adults and the young parasite remains alone in the nest. Young cuckoos are capable, only a few hours after hatching, of pushing out of the nest everything that is in it, eggs or other chicks. The common cuckoo has acquired a very specific adaptation that allows it to parasitize effectively the numerous passerines that can be its hosts. There are several races of common cuckoo that are distinguished only by the coloration of their eggs. Color variation is important and, in fact, the eggs look almost identical to the eggs of the most commonly parasitized hosts. Thus, the cuckoo races are specialized to parasitize particular species. This cuckoo even learns the song of its adoptive parents. Parasites of the Viduidae family benefit from a similar adaptation. Their chicks closely resemble, in plumage, beak color, posture, and call, the chicks of their hosts and go even more unnoticed.

🚨
It's mind-boggling to see how many young Americans, particularly those ages 18–24, reportedly view Sharia law favorably over the American constitutional system. It makes me question what they're actually being taught.

The education system has changed dramatically since those of us now in our 40s and older went through school. Phonics and phonemic awareness were pushed aside in many schools - now kids can't read, historical education has increasingly become politicized, and difficult parts of world history are often softened, omitted, or presented primarily through the lens of how they might make students feel rather than the historical facts themselves.

How many of today's graduates actually understand the history of Islamic expansion, the centuries of Muslim rule in Spain, the Islamic slave trade, or the historical conflicts between Islamic and Christian civilizations? How many understand the distinction between religious law and a constitutional government? You cannot make informed decisions about systems of government when you haven't been taught their histories, principles, and consequences.

We've also moved increasingly toward teaching subjective interpretations of history rather than establishing the facts and allowing students to critically evaluate them. There's a difference between acknowledging historical injustices and rewriting history through a modern political lens. There's also a difference between understanding another culture and romanticizing a system of government without understanding what it entails.

And let's be clear: Sharia is not simply another version of American law. A system governed by traditional interpretations of Sharia does not operate on the same principles of individual liberty, religious freedom, equality under the law, and constitutional protections that Americans enjoy. Supporting something without understanding its implications isn't informed tolerance.

I also think we've lost sight of what made America fundamentally different. Over the last century, lawmakers have increasingly expanded government authority, regulation, and bureaucracy. The country that once offered extraordinary opportunities for individuals to acquire land, build, work, and pursue their own version of the American dream has gradually become a place where people feel increasingly governed, restricted, and dependent on government rather than empowered by their own freedoms.

The Constitution was designed to limit government power and protect individual liberty, not give government unlimited authority over our lives.

Meanwhile, our media increasingly influences which historical facts and perspectives are considered acceptable to discuss. Criticism of religious or political ideologies is too often conflated with hatred toward the people who practice them. Understanding history requires being willing to examine ALL of it, including the uncomfortable parts.

We were raised with "sticks and stones may break my bones, but words will never hurt me." Yet somehow, in 2026, we've reached a point where words are increasingly being labeled as violence, while actual physical violence is sometimes excused or justified because someone claims to have been offended by what another person said. That's completely backwards. Being offended does not give anyone the right to assault, threaten, or physically harm another person. Freedom of speech means being able to express yourself, challenge authority, criticize your government, and disagree with others, even when your words are unpopular or uncomfortable. You cannot have a free society that increasingly polices speech while simultaneously making excuses for people who commit actual violence. That's the very opposite of the individual liberties and protections a constitutional republic was designed to preserve.

You cannot protect the next generation's freedoms by keeping them uninformed about the very things those freedoms protect them from.
